items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Jelly Roll would stand out in front of the club and talk to all these defeated musicians; half of them couldn't play, including me. We'd stand around there waiting for a gig and looking up at Jelly Roll.

ctx.x: He was kind of tall, and he smiled all the time. But he had a strange name. He would be in there. And James P. Johnson would come through there. Fats Waller come through there.

Jelly Roll stood on the corner. They didn't understand Jelly Roll. Jelly Roll would be talkin' like he talked to night people, who understand Jelly Roll... Jelly Roll would stand out in front of the club and talk to all these defeated musicians; half of them couldn't play, including me. We'd stand around there waiting for a gig and looking up at Jelly Roll. Well, Jelly Roll is from home. But Jelly Roll, he loves an audience. items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: About a dozen occasions I got the band. Home Town got a band for Jelly Roll.

ctx.x: Great piano player. He entertained. He had been doing that, man, for gangs of years. He’d play a party, and he would . . . the girls, the people would come over and shake his hand. Some of them would kiss him on the forehead. “Oh, Mr. Luckey.” “We’re so happy to play this party. Last time I played for you was for your sister’s wedding, not your wedding.” Or your aunt’s, and your cousin had a christening, a birthday party, that kind of crap. Played for him, Luckey Roberts.
